questions.stem: The degree of the polynomial \(P(x) = 6x^4-4x^3+3x^5-x+1\) is:
questions.hint: The degree is the highest power of \(x\) appearing — rewrite the terms in descending order first.

questions.stem: Which of the following shows the graph of a cubic function with leading coefficient of −3?
questions.hint: A cubic with a negative leading coefficient rises on the left and falls on the right. It has opposite end behaviour.

steps.explain: A cubic has odd degree, so its two ends point in opposite directions.
steps.work: For large |x|, the leading term −3x³ controls the graph.

steps.explain: Because the leading coefficient is negative, the left end rises and the right end falls.
Only diagram B has this end behaviour and a cubic shape.

keyPoints.note: Use the end behaviour determined by the leading term −3x³.

questions.hint: Expand the left side, then compare the coefficients of \(x\) and the constant terms with the right side.

steps.explain: Expand the left side: multiply each term of the first bracket by each term of the second.
Compare the constant terms (no \(x\)): \(-2k=10\).
Compare the coefficients of \(x\): \(k-2=a\). Substitute \(k=-5\).
Check by expanding with \(k=-5\): \((x-2)(x-5)=x^{2}-7x+10\) ✓ (\(a=-7\), constant 10).
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.note: Expand, then match the constant terms and the x terms.

questions.stem: Four identical squares are cut from the corners of a rectangular sheet of metal \(10\) cm \(\times\) \(8\) cm. The sides are folded along the dotted lines to form a rectangular box, as shown. Using the graph below find the appropriate side length(s) of the square that could be cut from each corner if the volume is to be \(48\ \text{cm}^{3}\).
questions.hint: Draw a HORIZONTAL line at \(V=48\) and read the \(x\)-values where it meets the curve. Then decide which are POSSIBLE: the box dimensions \(10-2x\) and \(8-2x\) must stay positive, so \(x\) must be less than \(4\).

steps.explain: Draw the line \(V=48\) across the graph. It meets the curve at three points, at about \(x=1\), \(x=2\) and \(x=6\).
Check by substituting: \(x=1\): \(8\times6\times1=48\) ✓; \(x=2\): \(6\times4\times2=48\) ✓; \(x=6\): \(-2\times(-4)\times6=48\) (mathematically true).
But a real box needs positive sides: \(8-2x>0\Rightarrow x<4\). For \(x=6\) the width would be \(8-12=-4\) (impossible).
So only \(x=1\) cm or \(x=2\) cm are possible side lengths for the cut square.
Why not the others: B and C include \(x=6\) (an impossible negative width); D leaves out \(x=1\).
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.text: find the appropriate side length(s) of the square

questions.stem: Sketch this factorised polynomial, showing all important features. \(y=-x^{4}(x-7)^{3}(x+8)^{2}(x-3)\)
questions.hint: For a factorised polynomial: each factor gives an \(x\)-intercept. An EVEN power (\(x^{4}\), \((x+8)^{2}\)) makes the graph TOUCH the axis and turn back; an ODD power (\((x-7)^{3}\), \((x-3)^{1}\)) makes it CROSS. The leading term decides the ends.

steps.explain: Intercepts: \(x=0\) (power 4), \(x=7\) (power 3), \(x=-8\) (power 2), \(x=3\) (power 1).
Even powers \(\Rightarrow\) TOUCH: at \(x=0\) and \(x=-8\) the curve touches the axis and does not cross. Odd powers \(\Rightarrow\) CROSS: at \(x=3\) and \(x=7\) it crosses.
Ends: the leading term is \(-x^{4}\cdot x^{3}\cdot x^{2}\cdot x=-x^{10}\): degree 10 (even) with a NEGATIVE coefficient, so BOTH ends go DOWN.

Sign between the intercepts: for large \(x>7\) the graph is negative, crossing up at 7?? — going back from the right: negative for \(x>7\), POSITIVE between \(3\) and \(7\) (cross at 7), NEGATIVE between \(0\) and \(3\) (cross at 3), and the touching points \(0\) and \(-8\) keep it negative on both sides.
Why not the others: B crosses at \(x=0\) (the even power should touch); C has both ends UP (wrong sign); D has the hump below the axis between 3 and 7.
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.text: Sketch this factorised polynomial, showing all important features.
keyPoints.note: Even power: touch; odd power: cross; degree 10 and \(-\): ends down.

topics.title: The remainder theorem and factor theorem

questions.stem: The remainder when \(3x^3-7x^2+2x+4\) is divided by \((x-3)\) is:
questions.hint: By the remainder theorem, the remainder equals \(P(3)\).

steps.explain: By the remainder theorem, substitute \(x=3\) into the polynomial.
Evaluate.

questions.stem: (b) When the polynomial \(P(x)=x^3-ax^2+x\) is divided by \((x-3)\), the remainder is 12. Find the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x+1)\).
questions.hint: Use the remainder theorem: substitute \(x=3\) to find \(a\), then substitute \(x=-1\) into \(P(x)\) to find the required remainder.

steps.explain: By the remainder theorem, \(P(3)=12\). Substitute and solve for \(a\).
Solve for \(a\).
Now find the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x+1)\), which by the remainder theorem is \(P(-1)\).
Evaluate.

questions.hint: Factor out 3, test x=1, and factor the remaining quadratic.

steps.explain: Remove the common factor 3.
Test x=1 and divide by (x−1).

questions.stem: If \(P(x)=3x^3-7x^2+2x+4\), divide \(P(x)\) by \(x-3\). Give your answer in the form \(P(x)=Q(x)(x-3)+R(x)\).
questions.hint: Set the divisor \(x-3\) equal to zero to find the synthetic value. Bring down the first coefficient, then multiply by \(3\) and add at each column. The last result is the remainder.

steps.explain: For synthetic division, first find the value that makes the divisor zero. Then write the coefficients of the dividend in descending powers of \(x\), including a coefficient for every power.
Bring down the leading coefficient \(3\). Multiply it by the synthetic value \(3\), then add that product to the next coefficient \(-7\).
Use the new bottom value \(2\). Multiply it by \(3\), then add the product to the next original coefficient \(2\).
Multiply the latest bottom value \(8\) by \(3\), then add the product to the final original coefficient \(4\). The final bottom value is the remainder.
The bottom row before the final number gives the quotient coefficients, in descending powers. The final number is the remainder.
Check by multiplying out the quotient times the divisor and then adding the remainder. The result must match the original polynomial.

keyPoints.note: Use synthetic value \(3\) because \(x-3=0\) when \(x=3\). The final synthetic-division result is the remainder.

questions.stem: Given \(P(x)=2x^{3}+x^{2}-5x+2\) and \(Q(x)=x+2\). What is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(Q(x)\)?
questions.hint: Remainder theorem: the remainder on dividing by \(x-a\) is \(P(a)\). Here \(x+2=x-(-2)\), so find \(P(-2)\).

steps.explain: Write \(x+2\) as \(x-(-2)\): \(a=-2\). The remainder is \(P(-2)\).
Substitute \(x=-2\) (careful with the signs of the powers: \((-2)^{3}=-8\), \((-2)^{2}=4\)).
Add.
The remainder is 0, so \((x+2)\) is a factor of \(P(x)\) (factor theorem), which we use in the next part.
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.note: Remainder theorem: substitute the root of the divisor.

questions.stem: Given \(P(x)=2x^{3}+x^{2}-5x+2\), which has the factor \(x+2\). Express \(P(x)\) as a product of its factors.
questions.hint: Divide \(P(x)\) by \((x+2)\) (long division) to get the quadratic quotient, then factorise it completely.

steps.explain: Factorise the quadratic \(2x^{2}-3x+1\): numbers with product \(2\times1=2\) and sum \(-3\) are \(-2\) and \(-1\): \(2x^{2}-2x-x+1=2x(x-1)-(x-1)\).
Full factorisation (option D is NOT complete, it still contains a factorisable quadratic).
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.note: Divide by the known factor, then factorise the quotient completely.

questions.stem: Hence or otherwise sketch \(y=P(x)\) showing \(x\) and \(y\)-intercepts, where \(P(x)=2x^{3}+x^{2}-5x+2=(x+2)(2x-1)(x-1)\). Which sketch (A, B, C or D in the figure) is correct?
questions.hint: \(x\)-intercepts from the factors; \(y\)-intercept \(=P(0)\) (the constant term); the leading term \(2x^{3}\) is positive, so the graph goes from bottom-left to top-right.

steps.explain: \(x\)-intercepts: set each factor to 0: \(x+2=0\), \(2x-1=0\), \(x-1=0\). Three single roots, so the curve crosses the axis at each (green).
\(y\)-intercept: \(P(0)=2\) (the constant term), the orange point \((0,2)\).
End behaviour: the \(x^{3}\) coefficient is \(+2>0\), so \(y\to+\infty\) as \(x\to\infty\) and \(y\to-\infty\) as \(x\to-\infty\) (bottom-left to top-right).

Shape: coming up from the bottom-left it crosses at \(-2\), rises to a local maximum, comes down through \((0,2)\)... then crosses \(x=\dfrac{1}{2}\), dips to a local minimum and crosses at \(x=1\) going up.
steps.work: \(\text{cross at }-2,\ \dfrac{1}{2},\ 1\ \text{with a max then a min}\)

steps.explain: Compare options: B is upside-down (negative leading coefficient); C has roots at \(2,-\dfrac{1}{2},-1\) (signs wrong); D is shifted down (\(y\)-intercept \(-2\)). Only A matches.
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.note: Roots from the factors, y-intercept from the constant term, ends from the sign of the x cubed term.

questions.stem: When \(P(x)=kx^{3}-2x^{2}+2x-3\) is divided by \((x+2)\), the remainder is \(1\). Find the value of \(k\).
questions.hint: REMAINDER THEOREM: the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x-a)\) is \(P(a)\). Here the divisor is \(x+2=x-(-2)\), so the remainder is \(P(-2)=1\). Substitute \(x=-2\) carefully (brackets!) and solve for \(k\).

steps.explain: Divisor \(x+2\): the value is \(x=-2\). Remainder theorem: \(P(-2)=1\).
Simplify: \(-8k-8-4-3=1\Rightarrow-8k-15=1\).
Add 15, then divide by \(-8\).
Check: \(P(-2)=-2(-8)-8-4-3=16-15=1\) ✓. Why not the others: \(k=2\) loses the sign; \(k=-1\) and \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) come from arithmetic slips in \(-8k-15=1\).
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.text: the remainder is \(1\). Find the value of \(k\).

questions.stem: Divide the polynomial \(P(x)=2x^{7}-x^{4}+x-4\) by \(x^{3}+3x\). Express answer in the form \(P(x)=A(x)Q(x)+R(x)\).
questions.hint: Polynomial LONG DIVISION: divide the leading terms, multiply back, SUBTRACT (change all signs), bring down, repeat until the remainder has lower degree than the divisor (degree \(<3\)). Insert \(0x^{6},0x^{5},0x^{3},0x^{2}\) for missing powers.

steps.explain: Divide the leading terms: \(2x^{7}\div x^{3}=2x^{4}\). Multiply back: \(2x^{4}(x^{3}+3x)=2x^{7}+6x^{5}\). Subtract: \(-6x^{5}-x^{4}+x-4\).
Next: \(18x^{3}\div x^{3}=18\). Multiply back: \(18(x^{3}+3x)=18x^{3}+54x\). Subtract: \(3x^{2}-53x-4\) (degree 2 \(<\) 3: STOP, this is the remainder).
Write \(P=A\times Q+R\) with divisor \(A(x)=x^{3}+3x\), quotient \(Q(x)=2x^{4}-6x^{2}-x+18\), remainder \(R(x)=3x^{2}-53x-4\).

Why not the others: B, C and D change one sign (in the remainder or in the quotient) — expanding them does not return \(P(x)\). (Note: the printed answer writes the divisor as \(x^{2}+3x\); the question's divisor is \(x^{3}+3x\).)
So the correct choice is option A.

questions.stem: Show that \((x+3)\) is a factor of \(P(x)=x^{3}-2x^{2}-9x+18\).
questions.hint: FACTOR THEOREM: \((x-a)\) is a factor of \(P(x)\) if and only if \(P(a)=0\). For \((x+3)=(x-(-3))\) test \(a=-3\) (the OPPOSITE sign) and use brackets with the negative number.

steps.explain: The remainder is 0, so by the factor theorem \((x+3)\) IS a factor ✓. Why not the others: B tests \(P(3)\) (that shows \(x-3\)); C concludes the wrong factor; D makes a sign error (\(-2(-3)^{2}\) became \(+18\)).
So the correct choice is option A.

questions.stem: \(P(x)=x^{3}-2x^{2}-9x+18\) and \((x+3)\) is a factor. Hence, using division find all the linear factors of \(P(x)\).
questions.hint: Divide \(P(x)\) by \((x+3)\) to get a QUADRATIC quotient. Factorise that quadratic into two more linear factors, and list all three.

steps.explain: Divide \(-5x^{2}\) by \(x\): \(-5x\). Multiply back \(-5x(x+3)=-5x^{2}-15x\), subtract: \(6x+18\).
Divide \(6x\) by \(x\): \(6\). Multiply back \(6(x+3)=6x+18\), subtract: \(0\) (no remainder ✓).
Factorise the quotient: numbers with product \(6\), sum \(-5\): \(-2\) and \(-3\).
All the linear factors.
Why not the others: B has \(x+2\) (sign error); C repeats \((x+3)\); D does not match \(P(0)=18\) (\(-3\times-2\times-1=-6\)).
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.text: using division find all the linear factors of \(P(x)\)

questions.stem: \(P(x)=x^{3}-2x^{2}-9x+18=(x+3)(x-2)(x-3)\). Draw a neat sketch of \(y=P(x)\) showing all intercepts.
questions.hint: Use the factorised form: the \(x\)-intercepts are where each bracket is 0; the \(y\)-intercept is \(P(0)\); the leading term \(+x^{3}\) means the graph starts LOW on the left and ends HIGH on the right.

steps.explain: \(x\)-intercepts (each bracket \(=0\)): \(x=-3,\ 2,\ 3\) — the graph crosses the axis at each (single factors).
End behaviour: leading coefficient \(+1>0\) and degree 3 (odd): down on the left, up on the right.
Join: from the bottom left, up through \((-3,0)\), over a hill through \((0,18)\), down through \((2,0)\) into a small dip, and up through \((3,0)\).

Why not the others: B is upside down (negative leading coefficient) and has \(y\)-intercept \(-18\); C has intercepts \(-3,-2,3\); D touches the axis at \(x=2\) (a repeated factor) with \(y\)-intercept \(12\).
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.text: Draw a neat sketch of \(y=P(x)\) showing all intercepts.
keyPoints.note: Intercepts \(-3,2,3\) and \(18\); odd degree, positive: low left, high right.
